topic.name: The Recursive Formula for a Geometric Sequence

question.text: What is the $5$th term of the geometric sequence given below? \[ f(n+1) = -\dfrac{1}{2}f(n),\quad f(1) = 80,\quad n\geq 1 \]
question.explanation:
We use the recursive formula to compute the terms of the sequence up to the $5$th term:

\begin{align*} f(1) &= 80\\[5pt] f(2) &= -\dfrac{1}{2}f(1) = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left(80\right) = -40\\[5pt] f(3) &= -\dfrac{1}{2}f(2) = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left(-40\right) = 20 \\[5pt] f(4) &= -\dfrac{1}{2}f(3) = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left(20\right) = -10 \\[5pt] f(5) &= -\dfrac{1}{2}f(4) = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left(-10\right) = 5 \end{align*}

Therefore, $f(5)=5.$

example.title: Calculating a Term of a Geometric Sequence Given a Recursive Formula in Function Notation

question.text:
Which of the three sequences below are geometric sequences?

  1. $\dfrac 14, \: \dfrac 12, \: 2, \: \dots$
  2. $a_{n+1} = \dfrac{3}{2}a_n,\quad a_1 = -1,\quad n\geq 1$
  3. $1, \: 0.2, \: 0.03, \: \dots$
question.explanation:
A sequence is geometric if there is a common ratio between its terms. Let's check each sequence in turn.

  • Sequence I is not a geometric sequence because not every pair of consecutive terms has the same ratio. To see this, we only need to go up to the third term: \begin{align*} \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac 12\right)}{\left(\dfrac 14\right)} &= 2 \\[5pt] \dfrac{a_3}{a_2}= \dfrac{2}{\left(\dfrac 12\right)} &= 4 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

  • Sequence II is a geometric sequence. The recursive rule $a_{n+1} = \dfrac{3}{2}a_n$ tells us that each term is $\dfrac{3}{2}$ times the previous term, so the common ratio is $r=\dfrac{3}{2}.$

  • Sequence III is not a geometric sequence because not every pair of consecutive terms has the same ratio. To see this, we only need to go up to the third term: \begin{align*} \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \dfrac{0.2}{1} &= 0.2 \\[5pt] \dfrac{a_3}{a_2}= \dfrac{0.03}{0.2} &= 0.15 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

In conclusion, only sequence II is a geometric sequence.

question.text: What is the $4$th term of the geometric sequence given below? \[ a_{n+1} = -6a_{n},\qquad a_{1} = \dfrac{1}{36},\qquad n\geq 1 \]
question.explanation:
We use the recursive formula to compute the terms of the sequence up to the $4$th term: \begin{align} a_{1} &= \dfrac{1}{36}\\[5pt] a_{2} &= -6 a_{1} = -6\left(\dfrac{1}{36}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{6}\\[5pt] a_{3} &=-6a_{2} = -6\left(-\dfrac{1}{6}\right) = 1 \\[5pt] a_{4} &= -6a_{3} =-6(1)= -6 \end{align}

Therefore, $a_{4}=-6.$
